description.narrative:
The proposed action, Somalia Humanitarian Integrated Project (SHIP) 2, aims to deliver integrated, life-saving humanitarian assistance to vulnerable and conflict-affected populations across targeted districts in Jubaland and South West States of Somalia.The project will address critical humanitarian needs arising from recurrent drought, displacement, disease outbreaks, food insecurity, and limited access to essential services through a multi-sectoral approach integrating Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Disaster Preparedness interventions.The project will focus on increasing the availability, accessibility, and utilisation of quality primary healthcare, nutrition, and WASH services in underserved and hard-to-reach communities, including internally displacedpersons (IDPs), returnees, women and girls, children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and persons with disabilities. Interventions will include provision of preventative and curative healthcare services, management of acute malnutrition, maternal and child health support, immunisation, disease surveillance, infection prevention and control, hygiene promotion, safe water access, sanitation improvements, and emergency preparedness measures.
The action will be implemented through a consortium led by World Vision Germany together with OxfamNovib and Medair, in partnership with local organisations including ZAMZAM Foundation, GREDO, WASDA, DAWA, and Vision Corps Initiative. The consortium will work closely with community structures, health authorities, and humanitarian coordination platforms to ensure effective, accountable, and community-led implementation.The project will target districts including Afmadow, Jamaame, Buale, Jilib, Badhaadhe, Afgooye, Bardhere, Diinsoor, Qansaxdhere, and Burhakaba, where humanitarian needs remain severe and access to integrated services is limited. Through strengthened community engagement, referral systems, and anticipatory action mechanisms, the project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality while enhancingcommunity resilience to future shocks and disease outbreaks.Gimme a little more details Project DescriptionThe Somalia Humanitarian Integrated Project (SHIP) 2 is a 12-month integrated humanitarian response project designed to address the urgent health, nutrition, WASH, and disaster preparedness needs of vulnerable populations affected byrecurrent drought, displacement, conflict, and disease outbreaks across Jubaland and South West States of Somalia. The project seeks to reduce morbidity and mortality among crisis-affected communities by improving access to quality, life-saving services in underserved and hard-to-reach areas.
The project will specifically target internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, women and girls, children under five, pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly persons, and people living with disabilities in the districts of Afmadow, Jamaame, Buale, Jilib, Badhaadhe, Afgooye, Baardheere, Diinsoor, Qansaxdhere, and Burhakaba. The intervention is expected todirectly benefit over 141,000 people through integrated service delivery and community-based approaches.Under the health component, the project will strengthen access to preventative and curative primary healthcare services through support to 14 health facilities and community outreach systems. Services will include outpatient consultations, maternal and child healthcare, immunisation, disease surveillance, emergency referrals, mental health and psychosocial support, management of communicable diseases, and integrated community case management (iCCM+) for malaria, diarrhoea, and respiratory infections among children under five. The project will also strengthen infection prevention and control systems, digital health information management, and capacity building forhealth workers and community health volunteers.The nutrition component will focus on the prevention, identification, referral, and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women. Activities will include community-based malnutrition screening using Family MUAC approaches, treatment of severe acute malnutrition, nutrition counselling, infant and young child feeding (IYCF) promotion, mother-to-mother support groups, cooking demonstrations, and strengthened referral pathways forspecialised care and multi-purpose cash assistance through collaboration with the Cash Consortium.The WASH component will improve access to safe water, sanitation, hygiene promotion, and infection prevention and control services at both health facility and community levels.
The project will rehabilitate and strengthen WASH infrastructure in supported health facilities, improve medical waste management systems, distribute hygiene and menstrual hygiene kits to vulnerable households, and conduct community awareness campaigns on hygiene and disease prevention. Community hygiene promoters and local health committees will play a key role in strengthening disease surveillance and promoting safe hygiene practices.The action will also incorporate disaster preparedness and anticipatory action mechanisms to enable early response to drought, disease outbreaks, displacement, and other climate-related shocks. Through community engagement, local coordination systems, and early warning mechanisms, the project will strengthen resilience and improve the ability of communities and service providers to respond to future emergencies.
The project will be implemented by a consortium led byWorld Vision Germany in partnership with Oxfam Novib and Medair, together with local implementing partners including ZAMZAM Foundation, GREDO, WASDA, DAWA, and Vision Corps Initiative. The consortium will work closely with community structures, local authorities,health ministries, and humanitarian coordinationplatforms to ensure accountable, inclusive, and community-led implementation of activities.

participating-org.narrative: WASDA was established as a nongovernmental in Somalia in 2001. The organisation strives to supplement the efforts of governments and other development stakeholders in addressing developmental challenges in the Horn of Africa. WASDA is currently implementing development initiatives in North-Eastern Kenya and parts of Southern Somalia. WASDA has been working with pastoral communities in North-Eastern Kenya and Southern Somalia for 23 years. The organisation has, in the process, gained and built a wealth of experience and knowledge that informs its programming. It utilises limited resources to change the lives of millions of people in its geographical areas of operation. In the last 23 years, WASDA has reached over 1.5 million people with livelihood, food security; water; sanitation and hygiene; health and nutrition; education and emergency humanitarian support. VISION Empowered communities in the Horn of Africa that are resilient, innovative and peaceful MISSION To mobilize and engage communities and other stakeholders in creating strategic partnerships for sustainable management of the environment, water resources, livelihoods, and education and public health services in the Horn of Africa.
